key_insight: An energy-structure-preserving finite element scheme delivers mesh-independent stability for rotating MHD-Boussinesq flows with nonlinear power-law viscosity.
engineering_relevance: The method supports stable simulation of coupled flow, heat transfer, and magnetic effects in rotating electrically conducting fluids.
method: Combine conforming velocity–temperature elements, Nédélec magnetic elements, and semi-implicit backward Euler time stepping.
Preserve exact Lorentz–induction energy cancellation and energy-neutral Coriolis forcing.
Use time-translate compactness and a Minty argument to analyse convergence and identify nonlinear diffusion.
evidence_signal: Three-dimensional numerical experiments confirm predicted stability and convergence, alongside a priori error estimates requiring no mesh–time coupling.
watch_item: Genuine weak-solution identification is established only in the Newtonian case and above an explicit three-dimensional power-law threshold imposed by the Lorentz force.
paper_title: Finite Element Approximation of Rotating MHD-Boussinesq Flows with Nonlinear Power-Law Viscosity
